A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SpecEval study. The main experiments and extensive specification appendices can be matched across versions. Text extraction and visual inspection resolve pagination and overflowing appendix text sufficiently for reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original adherence evaluations of 16 models across three provider specifications, qualitative response analyses, and a human-validation study with 60 responses and three annotators.

after.justification: v2 retains original model-adherence results, qualitative examples, judge comparisons, and the human-validation results in Appendix F.

M1.justification: The TestMaker–Candidate–Judge pipeline, adaptive generation procedure, Likert scoring, final binary evaluation, and Algorithm 1 remain unchanged. Missing prompt listings in v2 reduce documentation but do not establish a different method.

E1.justification: Both evaluate the same 2,360 prompts covering 46 OpenAI, 49 Anthropic, and 23 Google/Sparrow statements. The specification appendices retain all 118 statement IDs. No new evaluated domain, task, or population is reported.

E2.justification: The experimental setup and Appendix E retain the same 16 candidate models from six providers and the same three model judges. No comparison method is added or replaced; removal of a results display does not establish a changed evaluated roster.

E3.justification: Prompt counts, generation rounds, selection threshold, token limits, and human-study design remain unchanged. v2's explicit mention of greedy decoding restates the temperature-zero setting already documented in v1's Appendix B. Its separate presentation of same-provider scores uses an evaluation configuration already present in v1.

E4.justification: The model-version comparisons remain as v1 Figure 5 and v2 Figure 6. Judge-variation analyses, human-agreement tables, and refusal-style and CPR case studies also remain. Some explanatory prose disappears, but these analyses and their underlying comparisons are retained.

E5.justification: v1 Figure 6 reports standard errors and 95% confidence intervals for all 16 models across three specifications. v2 removes this entire figure without an equivalent uncertainty display. Its checklist still claims such reporting, but the displayed intervals are absent. Neither version supplies new repeated-run or seed information.

E6.justification: Removing v1 Figure 6 eliminates the comprehensive aggregate scores and rankings across all 16 models and three specifications; the retained six-model heatmap preserves only part of that result coverage. v2 also revises the headline Anthropic/OpenAI scores from 0.84/0.74 to 0.816/0.759 using the same-provider scores already shown in v1 Figure 5, not demonstrated performance gains. v2 Figure 4 shows Google at 0.680, while Section 4.2 retains 0.64.

T1.justification: The problem formulation and Cohen's kappa equations are retained. Three-way consistency was already defined conceptually in v1; its greater prominence in v2 adds no mathematical result, assumption, or proof.

C1.justification: Both claim a first systematic specification audit, an automated evaluation framework, a 2,360-prompt dataset, and substantial provider-consistency gaps. v2 foregrounds three-way consistency and itemizes contributions, but that focus and the substantive contributions were already present in v1.

C2.justification: v2 replaces the constitutional-training explanation for cross-specification adherence with a more qualified interpretation based on differing specification emphases. It adds an explicit warning about optimizing incorrect proxy objectives and removes the proposed future evaluation of conflicting specification statements. The central refusal-style and imminent-harm interpretations remain.

D1.justification: v1 supplies both the Likert-judge-generation meta-prompt and the policy-compliance judge template. Both bodies disappear in v2, leaving an empty listing caption and an unresolved Appendix B reference. The explicit GitHub and Hugging Face access instructions are replaced by a Dataverse preview address for data, although the checklist still mentions code access. Core hyperparameters and model identifiers remain.

R1.justification: v2 adds five cited works: Gao et al. on reward overoptimization, Hutchinson et al., Perez et al., Wallach et al., and Weidinger et al. These broaden the evaluation and auditing context without substantially changing the claimed relationship to prior generator-validator consistency or AutoBencher.

P1.justification: The abstract and introduction are substantially recast around three-way consistency, contributions become a bullet list, auditing moves to the start of related work, the results discussion is shortened, and the conclusion is rewritten. A full NeurIPS checklist is inserted. Editorial defects include the abstract ending with the incomplete phrase 'gaps of up to 20'.

P2.justification: v2 adds a compact consistency heatmap using existing scores, removes the three-panel aggregate-results figure, redraws Figure 3 and the model-version plots, and rearranges the statement and judge heatmaps. Appendix tables are substantially reflowed, including heavily wrapped model names in the judge-cost table; an empty listing caption and a nearly blank taxonomy opening page also appear.

improvement.justification: v2 more clearly distinguishes same-provider consistency from averages over three judges. However, removing both prompt-template bodies and the comprehensive results figure with uncertainty weakens reproducibility and evidential transparency. The Google score also conflicts between Figure 4 and Section 4.2, and broken references remain. These losses outweigh the clearer framing, while the underlying study and most evidence remain intact.
